name: Boeing 737 Classic (-300/-400/-500)
summary: The 1980s-90s generation of the world's best-selling narrowbody, with the smaller CFM56-3 engines; US examples now fly mainly as freighters and charters.

wings: Low swept wing with plain tips on most; some have aftermarket blended winglets
engines: Two CFM56-3 turbofans tucked tight under the wing, with a flat-bottomed 'hamster pouch' intake that looks small and oval
fuselage: Narrowbody fuselage; the -400 is stretched, the -500 shortened
tail: Conventional tail with a dorsal fillet at the fin base and a short pointed tail cone

tellTales: Engines tucked tight under the wing with a flattened, oval look and a small diameter
Narrowbody with underwing engines and a plain swept wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The NG has larger, rounder engine nacelles and a bigger wing, usually with tall blended winglets; the Classic has smaller oval nacelles and mostly plain tips.
The MD-80 has rear-mounted engines and a T-tail; the 737 has engines slung under the wings.
The A320's engines are larger and rounder and its fuselage is bigger; the 737 Classic has small, flat-bottomed engines tucked tight under the wing.
The 757 is longer and slimmer with a tall nose gear and larger engines on tall struts; the 737 Classic is shorter with engines tucked tight to the wing.
